How to Build a Custom MCP Server with TypeScript and Zod

Published October 3, 2026 • 7 min read • Technical Tutorial

Need instant tool schemas?

Use our interactive visual builder to generate Zod tool code in 5 seconds.

Launch Builder

The Model Context Protocol (MCP), introduced by Anthropic, provides an open specification for connecting AI assistants like Claude Desktop, Antigravity, and Cursor to external tools, APIs, and databases.

1. Project Setup & Package Installation

Initialize a new Node.js project and install the official MCP SDK and Zod:

mkdir my-mcp-server && cd my-mcp-server
npm init -y
npm install @modelcontextprotocol/sdk zod
npm install -D typescript @types/node tsx

2. Writing the Server and Tools

Create src/index.ts and instantiate the McpServer:

import { McpServer } from "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/mcp.js";
import { StdioServerTransport } from "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/stdio.js";
import { z } from "zod";

const server = new McpServer({
  name: "weather-service",
  version: "1.0.0"
});

// Register Tool
server.tool(
  "get_forecast",
  "Fetches the 7-day weather forecast for a specified city name.",
  {
    city: z.string().describe("City name to fetch forecast for"),
    units: z.enum(["celsius", "fahrenheit"]).default("celsius").describe("Temperature unit")
  },
  async ({ city, units }) => {
    return {
      content: [
        {
          type: "text",
          text: `Weather forecast for ${city}: 22 degrees ${units}, sunny.`
        }
      ]
    };
  }
);

// Connect over Stdio Transport
const transport = new StdioServerTransport();
await server.connect(transport);

3. Why Descriptive Zod Schemas Matter

Unlike traditional REST APIs where developers read documentation, AI models read parameter .describe() strings to determine argument values. Omitting descriptions is the single biggest cause of function-calling hallucination.

4. Connecting to Claude Desktop

Open your claude_desktop_config.json and add your server definition:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "weather": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "tsx", "D:/my-mcp-server/src/index.ts"]
    }
  }
}

Restart Claude Desktop, click the hammer icon, and your custom tool is instantly callable!
